chunk_findings.detail: The regression test never creates or enters a Git worktree: `adopted` only does `(repo / ".ddflow").mkdir(exist_ok=True)` and returns the ordinary `repo` fixture. The bug being fixed is specifically `ddflow review` run *from inside a worktree*, but all tests here exercise only a normal adopted repo. If the unfixed code chooses the derived hostname identity only when the repo is a worktree, every assertion in this file can still pass on the unfixed code, so the test does not actually guard B-review-identity-from-worktree-ignores-as-agent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py:21 (`adopted`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_clean_identity` removes `DDFLOW_AGENT` and `CLAUDECODE` but not `AGENT_NAME`, even though the module doc explicitly calls out `AGENT_NAME` as an identity source that must not be lost. On a machine with `AGENT_NAME` exported, `Ctx.log.agent_id` in `test_detach_argv_redeclares_an_env_sourced_identity` and `test_detach_launches_with_the_resolved_identity` can resolve to the ambient `AGENT_NAME` value instead of the monkeypatched `DDFLOW_AGENT`, causing environment-dependent failures; conversely, no test ever sets `AGENT_NAME`, so a regression on the `AGENT_NAME`-only path (including its leading-dash case) stays green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py:17 (`_clean_identity`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `linked` fixture shells out to the real `git` binary via `subprocess.run` (`git commit` and `git worktree add`) instead of going through the git port in `ddflow/adapters`. This violates [r-adapters], which requires git/subprocess tools to sit behind one adapter and says tests should use a fake rather than a subprocess. A test environment that provides the adapter fake but no `git` executable makes `linked` raise `FileNotFoundError` before the identity assertion runs, so the regression test fails for an environment reason rather than testing the fix.
